title: How to Enrich Leads with Technographic Data Without ZoomInfo
summary: How to find a company's tech stack and enrich leads using BuiltWith, Wappalyzer, HG Insights, and job posting inference — without a ZoomInfo contract.
body_markdown:
## You Don't Need ZoomInfo to Enrich Leads with Technographic Data


ZoomInfo's technographic data is good. It is also expensive, bundled into a contract that most early-stage teams and lean RevOps setups cannot justify. The underlying signals ZoomInfo aggregates are largely available from purpose-built tools — BuiltWith, Wappalyzer, HG Insights, Bombora — plus free job posting inference and AI research agents, often at a fraction of the cost.


Orange Slice, a chat-first enrichment platform, is one tool that pulls these signals together. But this guide is not a pitch for any single product. It is a practical walkthrough of how to build a technographic enrichment workflow without a ZoomInfo subscription, which tools to use at each layer, and where the gaps are so you can fill them deliberately.


---


## What Technographic Data Actually Covers (and Where Are the Gaps?)


Before picking tools, be clear about what you are trying to detect. Tech stacks have layers:


Layer Examples Detectability Without ZoomInfo


Front-end / marketing stack Google Tag Manager, HubSpot tracking, Intercom widget High — browser tools read these directly


Ad and analytics platforms GA4, Segment, Meta Pixel, Heap High — visible in page source


E-commerce platform Shopify, Magento, WooCommerce High


CRM Salesforce, HubSpot, Dynamics Medium — job postings, partner pages


Marketing automation Marketo, Pardot, Eloqua Medium — job postings, G2 reviews


Data infrastructure Snowflake, dbt, Fivetran Low — rarely public-facing


ERP / back-end SAP, NetSuite, Workday Low — requires intent data or job inference


Browser-based detection tools are powerful for the top three rows. Everything below that requires a different approach.


---


## Which Tools Replace ZoomInfo for Technographic Data?


### Is BuiltWith worth it for tech stack detection?


BuiltWith crawls the public web and identifies technologies by reading JavaScript libraries, cookies, HTTP headers, and DNS records. It covers thousands of technologies and gives you historical data — meaning you can see when a company adopted or dropped a tool. BuiltWith's database tracks over 93,000 internet technologies across more than 673 million websites, according to[BuiltWith's own technology lookup documentation](https://builtwith.com/about) .


**Best for:** Marketing tech, ad platforms, e-commerce stacks, CDNs, front-end frameworks.
**Limitations:** No visibility into back-end software that leaves no public web trace. Enterprise CRM and ERP installs are largely invisible.
**Pricing model:** API access and bulk list exports require a paid plan. Individual lookups are free via the browser extension.


### How does Wappalyzer compare to BuiltWith?


Similar to BuiltWith but with a cleaner API and a browser extension that works in real time as you browse a prospect's site.[Wappalyzer](https://www.wappalyzer.com/) also offers a bulk enrichment API you can call programmatically.


**Best for:** Fast, lightweight technographic checks during prospecting. Good for SDRs who want to verify a prospect's stack before a call.
**Limitations:** Shallower historical data than BuiltWith. Same front-end bias.


### When should you use HG Insights instead?


[HG Insights](https://hginsights.com/) specializes in enterprise technology install data and intent signals. It covers CRM, ERP, cloud infrastructure, and security tooling — the layers that BuiltWith misses. It is a premium product priced accordingly, but it is purpose-built for technographics in a way that ZoomInfo is not.


**Best for:** Enterprise accounts where you need to confirm SAP, Salesforce, or Workday installs before investing in a deal.
**Limitations:** Cost. Not designed for high-volume SMB prospecting.


### What does Bombora add that install data tools don't?


[Bombora](https://bombora.com/) is primarily a B2B intent data platform, but its company surge data includes technology-related topics. If a company is researching "Salesforce migration" or "data warehouse vendors," Bombora surfaces that signal.


**Best for:** Catching accounts in active evaluation mode — they are looking to buy or switch, which is the best time to reach out.
**Limitations:** Intent data tells you what a company is *researching* , not necessarily what they *run* . Use it alongside install data, not instead of it.


### Can job postings replace paid technographic tools?


This is the most underused technographic signal available. When a company posts a job for a "Salesforce Administrator" or a "Marketo Specialist," they are telling you exactly what they run. A posting requiring "experience with dbt, Snowflake, and Fivetran" maps their entire data stack.


You can scrape job postings manually, use LinkedIn or Indeed searches, or automate it with an AI browser agent that visits a company's careers page and extracts tool mentions.


**Best for:** Mid-market and enterprise companies that post detailed job requirements.
**Limitations:** Companies with low hiring volume or that outsource roles may not post enough to infer their stack. Job postings lag reality by weeks or months.


---


## How to Build a Technographic Enrichment Workflow Without ZoomInfo


The goal is tech stack coverage at the lowest per-record cost. That means waterfall enrichment: query cheap sources first, escalate to premium sources only when you need to.


### Step 1: Start with Browser-Based Detection


Run your account list through BuiltWith or Wappalyzer's bulk API. For any company with a public web presence, this gives you front-end and marketing stack data immediately. Flag records where you got a confirmed match on your target technology (e.g., "runs HubSpot") and set them aside for outreach prioritization.


### Step 2: Parse Job Postings for Back-End Stack Signals


For accounts where browser detection returned nothing useful — or where you need to confirm CRM and ERP installs — pull their current job postings. An AI browser agent can visit a company's careers page, extract all open roles, and scan for tool mentions. This is free signal that most teams ignore.


[Orange Slice's workflow layer](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/workflows) supports exactly this kind of multi-step sequence: enrich with browser detection first, then trigger a job posting scrape only for accounts that need it, then write the result back to the same row.


### Step 3: Escalate to Intent Data for High-Value Accounts


For your top-tier target accounts — the ones where a single deal justifies significant research spend — layer in Bombora intent data or HG Insights install data. You are not doing this for every record. You are doing it for the fifty accounts in your named account list where you need to be certain before investing in a multi-touch sequence.


### Step 4: Gate Outreach on Tech Stack Confirmation


Do not enrich email and phone data until you have confirmed tech stack fit. This is where most teams waste credits. If your product requires Salesforce and the account runs Dynamics, you can disqualify them before spending anything on contact enrichment.


The[lead qualification workflow](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/lead-qualification-agent) is the right place to implement this gate: score or qualify on technographic fit first, then trigger contact enrichment only for accounts that pass.

## Where Does Orange Slice Fit (and Where Doesn't It)?


[Orange Slice](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/data-enrichment-agent) pulls tech stack signals as part of its enrichment layer — alongside firmographics, LinkedIn intelligence, verified emails, and hiring signals — in a single chat-first spreadsheet. You describe your ICP, and columns auto-populate. For accounts where job posting inference or AI web research can surface the stack, it works well.


What Orange Slice does not do: it is not a dedicated technographic database. It does not have the depth of install-base coverage that HG Insights provides for enterprise software. If your entire qualification model hinges on confirming a specific enterprise ERP install across thousands of accounts, you need HG Insights or a similar specialist vendor.


For teams that need technographic data as one signal among many — alongside contact data, firmographics, and hiring signals — Orange Slice handles the workflow without requiring separate tool subscriptions for each data type. Credits are charged only when data is found, which matters when you are running waterfall enrichment and many records will resolve at the cheap layers. See[pricing](https://www.orangeslice.ai/pricing) for how credits work.

## What's the Practical Starting Point?


If you are building this from scratch:


1. **Add the Wappalyzer browser extension** and use it during manual prospecting to verify stack before outreach — zero cost.
2. **Run your account list through BuiltWith's bulk API** to flag marketing and front-end tech at scale.
3. **Set up a job posting scrape** for accounts where browser detection is insufficient. An AI agent can do this automatically.
4. **Reserve HG Insights or Bombora** for your named account tier where install certainty matters.
5. **Gate contact enrichment on tech stack fit** — don't spend credits on email and phone data until you know the account qualifies.


The[use cases page](https://www.orangeslice.ai/use-cases) has concrete workflow examples for how teams put these signals together into outbound plays. If you want to see how a real customer operationalized enrichment at scale, the[Pirros case study](https://www.orangeslice.ai/case-studies/pirros) is worth reading.


The tools exist. The data is available. The only thing that makes ZoomInfo feel irreplaceable is not having a workflow that pulls from multiple sources automatically.
